issue.title: Teardown watchdog reaps Muse providers 120s after a declaration while the background work they are waiting on is still pending
issue.description:
The provider teardown watchdog kills Muse agents that are legitimately waiting for a background command their harness will wake them for, so verification dies, beads stay open, and the run is recorded as a clean success. Found while consolidating the headless early-exit research (research.29.final).

Root cause: `start_completion_watchdog` in `src/sase/llm_provider/_subprocess_plain.py` arms on any new `final_submission.json` and, 120 s later (`SASE_PROVIDER_TEARDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`), terminates the provider if the process is still alive. It checks liveness only: it never looks at whether the provider has background work pending or whether the model is mid-turn. Muse Code 1.3.0 (`muse exec`) keeps the process alive after the model ends its turn and wakes the model when a background command finishes (its Bash tool text: "the final output is delivered to you automatically as runtime context and wakes you even after you end the turn"). Meanwhile `/sase_final` (`src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_final.md:11`) and core memory `sase/memory/sase.md:77` tell agents to declare before an "I will wait" reply. So a Muse agent declares (commit, bead kept open), ends its turn to wait for its `just check` wake, and is killed 120 s later; Muse logs `Background terminal cancelled`.

Evidence (athena, Sep 20-22): all 9 `provider_teardown_stall.json` files in `~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run/202609/` are `runtime: muse`, and 8 of 9 final replies claim a pending wait (`sase-142.5.2`, `sase-142.5.3`, `sase-14n.4`, `sase-14n.9`, `sase-157.7`, `sase-15p.2`, `0pb--1`, `sase-16e.5`). The one exception (`sase-157.3`) was Muse's own end-of-turn reminder wait after the bead was closed. The watchdog's motivating incident (`plan:202609/provider_teardown_stall_watchdog.md`, `research.a.cdx`) was also a Muse run.

Fix direction: have the Muse stream parser (`_tool_call_muse.py`, which already sees `execution_state: background_running` and `Background terminal completed/failed/cancelled`) track outstanding background tasks, like `ClaudeTurnWaitState.outstanding_background_tasks`, and expose them to the watchdog (e.g. a per-run `provider_pending_work.json`). Reap only when a declaration is current AND nothing is pending AND the stream has been idle for the grace period. While work is pending, apply a separate long ceiling; when it fires, record the run as incomplete rather than a clean exit. Keep the 120 s path for the idle leaked-pipe case. Add unit tests covering a pending background task, a woken turn after declaration, and the idle-reap case. Optionally surface a distinct waiting state in the TUI.

task_type_fields.impact: The main active cause of Muse agents dying after long commands: work lands unverified, 3 beads (`sase-142.5.2`, `sase-142.5.3`, `sase-16e.5`) are still in_progress, and at least 3 more (`sase-14n.4`, `sase-14n.9`, `sase-15p.2`) had to be closed by hand as "completed but did not finish verification". Runs are recorded as SUCCESS. Details: research:202609/provider_wait_contract_early_exits/provider_wait_contract_early_exits.md §2.1 and §5 Step 1.1.
task_type_fields.repro: Run a Muse agent with an assigned bead that starts `sase tool run check` (Muse backgrounds it after its 10 s yield), submits a checkpoint declaration with the bead kept open, and ends its turn to wait for the wake. 120 s after the declaration the runner writes `provider_teardown_stall.json`, the check is cancelled, the bead stays in_progress, and the run is reported as a clean exit. Observed 8 times on athena Sep 20-22, most recently `sase-16e.5` (artifacts `ace-run/202609/22/20260922121459`, Muse session `97dbdd11`: final reply at 17:02:07Z, `background cancelled` at 17:04:03Z).

payload.description: Same false-success class: a run whose assigned bead is still open is recorded as plain success; the watchdog kill feeds it
Claude -p also has a bounded background wait (workflows/subagents) that this watchdog would cut off
Muse background-wait research: check status of related wait/monitor beads
